clue.text: A joy to travellers? Many birds nested in one

definitions.meaning: traveller's joy is the common name of the wild clematis, whose fluffy seed heads give it this other name
in Edward Lear's limerick an old man complains that two owls, a hen, four larks and a wren have all built their nests in his chin's growth

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the twisted plant name: 'traveller's joy' becomes 'a joy to travellers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the wild clematis is called traveller's joy, and Lear's nonsense verse has birds nesting in an old fellow's whiskers.

clue.text: Dim old boy found in certain clubs

parts.note: OB is the standard abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: found in says the clubs letter sits inside the word for certain

parts.note: certain means sure
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A former pupil turns up, unremarkable, in some particular clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim and obscure are synonyms for faint or hard to make out.

clue.text: Awfully bad rule that's likely to remain

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters of the next two words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A terrible regulation that looks set to stay in force.
explanation.definitionFit: Something durable lasts, so it is apt to stay around for a long time.

clue.text: Gentle pace an Old Testament tribe can outrun at first

parts.note: taken as written
Dan is one of the twelve tribes of Israel
a can is a tin

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the following word, outrun

explanation.surface: A biblical tribe, moving gently, manages to outpace someone at the start of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: In music this tempo marking means slightly quicker than a walking pace, a moderate speed.

clue.text: Having good taste, it's reported, without power

indicators.note: it's reported says the word for drained of strength is said aloud to give the answer's sound

parts.note: drained of strength is sapped

explanation.surface: Someone with refined palate is said to be powerless.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapid dish is flavoursome, pleasing to the palate.

clue.text: It may bring about the downfall of those on the rocks

definitions.text: It may bring about the downfall of those on the rocks

parts.words: It may bring about the downfall of those on the rocks
parts.note: reads like drink ruining people who take whisky on ice, but describes the gradual wearing away of cliffs that topples whatever stands on them

explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rocks' suggests drinks over ice or shipwreck; here it is literal, things standing on rock that wears away.
explanation.definitionFit: Weathering and wearing away of rock undermines and topples what is built or perched on it.

clue.text: Take over from chief magistrate, imprisoning just over 50

indicators.note: imprisoning says the magistrate word holds the numeral within it

parts.note: a reeve was the chief magistrate of a town or district in medieval England
LI is 51 in Roman numerals, one more than fifty

explanation.surface: A deputy succeeds a senior judge who has locked up about fifty people.
explanation.walkthrough: A reeve was a local official in Anglo-Saxon and medieval England.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone is to take their place on duty, as one sentry replaces another.

clue.text: Citizen investing little money in rebuilding of ruined villa

indicators.note: investing the coin in the shuffled letters means placing it inside them
rebuilding means the letters of ruined villa are put together in a new order

parts.note: P, for penny, is a small coin

explanation.surface: A local puts a bit of cash into restoring a wrecked country house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilding of' rearranges RUINED VILLA, and 'investing' puts P inside that mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A Liverpudlian is a citizen of Liverpool, the clue's definition standing for a resident of that city.

clue.text: Hardened sinner initially kept under cover

indicators.note: kept means held within, so the single letter is placed inside the word for hardened

parts.note: inured means hardened, accustomed to hardship

indicators.note: initially takes only the opening letter of the word sinner

explanation.surface: A habitual wrongdoer is first held under guard.
explanation.definitionFit: Being insured means having protection by a policy, as one is under cover.

clue.text: Poser, fitting odd bits of ballet into concert

indicators.note: into says the picked letters are fitted inside the concert word

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert

indicators.note: odd bits of picks the first, third and fifth letters of ballet

explanation.surface: A puzzle: how to fit some dance fragments into a concert programme.
explanation.walkthrough: A prom is one of London's summer promenade concerts, the BBC Proms.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a tricky question or puzzle needing a solution.

clue.text: Wrongly describe skinflint finally turning up with gift

indicators.note: finally turning up turns only the last two letters of the skinflint word, in a down clue reading upwards

parts.note: a skinflint is a miser
a gift is a present

explanation.surface: A miser at last arrives with a gift, and is misrepresented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally turning up' flips only the last two letters of MISER, giving MISRE; in a down clue 'up' suits a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To misrepresent is to give a false or misleading account of something.

clue.text: One-time pope living outside the city

parts.note: ex means former or one-time
Urban is the name of eight popes

explanation.surface: A former pontiff now lives beyond the town limits.
explanation.definitionFit: Exurban describes the area beyond the suburbs, the outer commuter belt.

clue.text: Birds with runs in woods

indicators.note: in puts the runs letter inside the birds

parts.note: divers are diving water birds, loons
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Birds and runs in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woods' looks like forest; it is golf clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, drivers are woods, the long-hitting clubs.

clue.text: Device for shooting rook, possibly

definitions.meaning: a rook is one example of a chessman

explanation.definitionFit: A gun is called a piece in slang, and a rook is one of the chessmen.

clue.text: Hypocritical Church Army members joining in moral offence

parts.note: taken as written
a sin is a moral offence
CE is the Church of England
RE, the Royal Engineers, are army soldiers

explanation.surface: A two-faced Salvation-style charity is caught up in wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Insincere and hypocritical both describe someone not meaning what they say.

clue.text: Takes away pamphlet accepted by editorial assistants

indicators.note: accepted by puts the pamphlet word inside the word for editorial assistants

parts.note: subs are subeditors on a newspaper
a tract is a short pamphlet

explanation.surface: Junior editors take a leaflet and remove some of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To subtract is to take away, as with numbers.

clue.text: Do some digging up in bed most needing to be turned over

indicators.note: needing to be turned over says the three words before it must be churned into a new order

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: the bed most needing work should be dug over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing to be turned over' rearranges IN BED MOST.
explanation.definitionFit: To disentomb is to exhume, digging something out of a grave.

clue.text: She should easily reach a high position on the staff

definitions.text: She should easily reach a high position on the staff

parts.words: She should easily reach a high position on the staff
parts.note: reads like a woman destined for promotion in an organisation, but the staff is the musical stave, and the high position is a high note

explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests employees; it is the five-line musical stave.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest female singing voice reaches notes placed high on the stave.

clue.text: Shopkeeper's granddaughter carrying bat adapted for game

indicators.note: carrying means the girl's name holds the shuffled letters inside

parts.note: Little Nell in Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop is the shopkeeper's granddaughter

indicators.note: adapted means the letters of bat are altered into another order

explanation.surface: A shop owner's grandchild carries a modified bat for sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Nell is the heroine of Dickens's novel; netball is a team ball game popular in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team game played with a ball and a high ring.

clue.text: Some chose the right solvent

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone picked the correct cleaning fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether is a volatile liquid used to dissolve fats and other substances.

clue.text: Raw material for paper assembled in seaport

indicators.note: assembled says the letters of seaport are put together afresh in a different order

explanation.surface: Paper's raw stock is gathered at a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Esparto is a tough grass used in making paper and rope.

clue.text: Cushion husband before a second blow

parts.note: a sock is a punch, a blow

explanation.surface: A spouse should be cushioned before taking another punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A hassock is a kneeling cushion in a church pew.

clue.text: Accredited claim that one's placed before top journalist?

parts.note: the claim I'm says that one is something
placed means put
ED, the editor, is the top journalist

explanation.surface: A credited assertion that one ranks above the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To be imputed is to be attributed or ascribed, as accredited means.

clue.text: Of haggard appearance, as lots are

definitions.meaning: tired-looking and pinched in the face
lots are pulled out of a hat to decide something

explanation.definitionFit: A haggard face is called drawn, and lots are drawn in a draw.

clue.text: Lies about affectations

parts.note: re means about, concerning
poses are affectations, put-on manners

explanation.surface: Someone tells untruths about their mannerisms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lies' looks like falsehoods; it means rests.
explanation.definitionFit: To repose is to lie at rest.

clue.text: A river with a secure backing? It's attraction is falling

indicators.note: backing reads all of the pieces before it in the opposite direction

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
to secure something is to gain it

explanation.surface: A river, gaining support: its appeal is its waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous falls on the US-Canada border are the great tourist draw of that river.

clue.text: Humorous drawing of unladen farm vehicle?

parts.note: a cart is a farm vehicle
unladen read as having nothing on: O, the zero for nothing, followed by on

explanation.surface: A cartoonist sketches an empty farm wagon for laughs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unladen' is read as 'nothing on': O plus ON. The question mark flags that playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic sketch in a newspaper or magazine is a funny picture.

clue.text: Very rich liquid for making soup in dining-cars, say

parts.note: rolling in it means very wealthy
stock is the broth used as a base for soup

explanation.surface: A rich broth served in the restaurant car of a train.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway carriages and wagons, dining cars included, are collectively the trains' movable vehicles.
